title: Fix converted subtitle codec verification
summary: Normalize converted subtitle verification expectations so an SRT input copied into the output is verified as the resulting subrip media codec instead of the FFmpeg command token copy.
reason: A representative Kanan encode completed video encoding and muxing but was blocked during output verification because converted ASS-to-SRT tracks used -c:s copy while the verifier incorrectly expected ffprobe to report codec_name=copy. ffprobe correctly reports subrip for that output stream.
behavior_before: Converted ASS, TX3G, BDPGS, and VobSub tracks could record copy as their expected output codec when the converted SRT input was stream-copied, causing valid subrip output streams to fail media-track verification.
behavior_after: Converted subtitle tracks still use the configured FFmpeg codec command, but verification maps copy to the resulting subrip codec while preserving explicit non-copy codec expectations.
tests_added: Invoke-SubtitleBuilderDecisionChecks.ps1 now covers converted ASS, TX3G, and BDPGS tracks when the FFmpeg output codec command is copy and requires subrip verification expectations.
manual_validation: A fresh real-media Kanan encode completed with exit code 0, passed duration and media-track verification, and published successfully.
GREEN: Invoke-SubtitleBuilderDecisionChecks.ps1 passed after the production change.
Invoke-ReliabilityRegressionChecks.ps1 passed the full active reliability regression suite.
Invoke-ToolIntegrationChecks.ps1 passed bundled FFmpeg, ffprobe, and subtitle integration checks.
PSScriptAnalyzer reported no errors for the changed PowerShell implementation and test.
RED: Invoke-SubtitleBuilderDecisionChecks.ps1 failed with expected subrip,subrip,subrip but actual copy,copy,copy before the production change.
The production verifier passed the retained failed Kanan encode artifact against its corrected in-memory plan with zero mismatches.
rollback_plan: Revert the verification-only expected-codec normalization and its regression test. Existing published media does not need to be changed; the rollback would restore the prior false-negative verification behavior for stream-copied converted SRT tracks.
notes:
Python impact: none. Source media was not mutated. Failure-marker clears were dry-run scoped first and manifest-backed; they did not touch media. No commit was created.
